data.reasoning: The deepseek model comprehensively reviewed all files and correctly identified that the package contains no malicious injections. It appropriately distinguished between packaging hygiene issues (unpinned MPM downloads, world-writable directories) and actual supply-chain threats, aligning perfectly with the threat model. The qwen model's inconclusive verdict was not based on security findings but rather on HTTP 400 API errors that prevented it from reviewing four of the five files. Since the deepseek model covered all files and found no injection patterns, the package is safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems entirely from a tool failure in the qwen model (HTTP 400 errors on 4 files), which forced an inconclusive result, whereas the deepseek model successfully processed all files and returned a safe verdict.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .SRCINFO, .gitignore, .nvchecker.toml, and matlab.install due to HTTP 400 API errors.
learnings: Implement retry logic for transient LLM API errors (e.g., HTTP 400) to prevent partial audits from triggering unnecessary escalations.

When secondary metadata files (.SRCINFO, .gitignore) fail to audit due to tool errors, the system should weigh the successful audit of critical execution files (PKGBUILD, .install) more heavily rather than defaulting to an inconclusive verdict.
